title: Dynamic telemetry rehydration for ephemeral tenants during incident windows
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Several enterprise customers reported dashboards showing zeroed or missing metrics and incomplete traces immediately after a cross-region capacity failover. Investigation shows ephemeral tenant token refreshes combined with aggressive metric TTLs caused data to be evicted from the ingest window and the rehydration path for short-lived tenants was not replaying buffered telemetry. This ticket implements a production-safe rehydration bridge: capture short-lived tenant telemetry metadata on failover, replay to ingestion with backfill markers, and surface a transient 'rehydration' state in the console until continuity is verified.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate regional outage: scale down ingest workers in region-eu and trigger smart-routing failover to region-us.
2) Spin up ephemeral tenant clients that use short-lived auth tokens (<= 5m) and burst telemetry (metrics + spans) during the failover window.
3) Observe console: metric tiles for these tenants show gaps or zero values; traces are missing child spans beyond the failover timestamp.
4) Confirm ingestion logs: TTL eviction and missing replay records for tenant IDs with prefix 'tmp-' in the rehydration buffer.
comments: 2026-03-09 Sofia Martinez: Initial customer escalation received from Acme Finance complaining about missing SLA dashboards after scheduled network maintenance in eu-west. Pager duty triggered. Assigned to Arjun.

2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Root cause hypothesis: ephemeral tokens expire mid-replay, rehydration path drops payload because auth-check fails; ingestion TTLs prune the metric index before replay completes. Captured spans and logs (s3://obs-archives/2026-03-09/acme-telemetry.tar.gz).

2026-03-11 Engineering sync: Decided to implement a two-pronged fix: (A) short-term: extend rehydration buffer TTL + bypass auth-check for trusted replay service; (B) long-term: add replay tokens and marker-based backfill semantics. Prioritizing (A) as emergency hotfix with feature flag.

2026-03-12 QA: Hotfix branch built and smoke-tested in staging with synthetic ephemeral tenants. Metrics reappeared within 45s of replay; trace stitching restored parent-child relationships in 70% of runs. Opening follow-up ENG tasks for remaining heurstic edge cases.

2026-03-13 Ops: Deployed hotfix to Hosted production behind feature flag; enabled for customers affected by the incident. Monitoring shows rehydration success and reduction in customer tickets. Noted a 3% CPU increase on ingest workers due to replay load — acceptable for short windows.
2026-03-14 PM review (Lena Huang): Customer communications drafted and queued; recommend status page update and targeted customer outreach for impacted tenants.
resolution_summary: Implemented a temporary rehydration bridge that extends the in-memory rehydration buffer to 10 minutes for flagged tenants, allows a trusted replay service to bypass token expiry for replayed payloads, and emits backfill markers consumed by the console to avoid zeroed tiles during the rehydration window. Hotfix rolled to production behind a feature flag; customer dashboards recovered. Follow-up work scheduled to harden replay auth and optimize replay resource usage.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix deployed behind feature-flag and enabled for impacted customers with no regressions in metric correctness for other tenants
Dashboards for previously affected ephemeral tenants display continuous time series with backfill markers within 2 minutes of replay completion
Trace stitching verifies >95% parent-child continuity for replayed spans in synthetic tests
Monitoring alerts added for rehydration buffer saturation and replay-auth bypass usage
follow_up_actions: ENG-48522: Replace auth-bypass with replay-token flow and rotate tokens per deployment
ENG-48523: Workload-aware replay throttling to avoid CPU surges on ingest workers
DOCS-191: Update runbook and incident response steps for cross-region telemetry failover
PM-492: Customer outreach & SLA credit evaluation for impacted tenants
